text: Virgil K Smith, born December 18, 1979, is a former Democratic member of the Michigan House of Representatives and Michigan Senate. He previously represented the 4th Senate district, which includes Allen Park, Lincoln Park, Southgate, and the north side of Detroit, and from 2003 to 2008 represented State House District 7, covering the northern tier of Detroit. Smith is the son of Virgil C. Smith, a retired Chief Judge of the Third Judicial Circuit of Michigan and former Michigan State Senator. In 2000, he was arrested for possessing alcohol while underage. In 2004, his license was revoked due to two alcohol-related offenses and was reinstated in 2008; in 2010, he was pulled over on DUI allegations but was not charged. On May 6, 2009, Smith married Anistia Thomas, but filed for divorce in July 2009, with Thomas counter-suing for annulment, which was granted on October 6, 2009. In May 2015, Smith was charged with felonious assault, domestic violence, malicious destruction of property, and felony firearm after shooting Thomas's car; Thomas was granted a Personal Protection Order as a result. In 2016, Smith pleaded guilty to malicious destruction of personal property, a felony, and was sentenced to ten months in prison. He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Michigan State University and a master's degree in public administration from Western Michigan University. Smith won the Democratic primary in 2002 against former state senator Henry Stallings II. In 2010, he was elected to the Michigan Senate, defeating George Cushingberry; he ran again in 2016 against Rashida Tlaib and was re-elected. In 2015, Smith pled guilty to malicious destruction of personal property after shooting at his ex-wife's car, leading to his resignation from the Senate. The plea deal initially required him to resign from office and not run for public office for five years, but a county circuit judge ruled that such a clause violated the state constitution. Smith ran for the Detroit City Council in 2017; the Wayne County prosecutor appealed the ruling on the plea deal, but the appeal was dismissed in April 2017. Smith finished second in the August primary, facing Roy McCalister Jr. on the general election ballot, and lost the general election to McCalister.
